correctness.summary: For every n>=2, set r=8/3, x_1=1/4 and x_2=...=x_n=1/16. With Q=prod x_i^(r x_i) and P=prod x_i, exact exponent arithmetic gives Q=2^(-(2n+2)/3) and (sum_i P^(r x_i))/Q=4^(1-n)+2(n-1). Since the conjectured left side divided by Q is n, the reversed gap is 4^(1-n)+n-2>0 for all n>=2. Also e>1+1+1/2+1/6=8/3, so r is admissible. The two-level reduction n>=a^((n-1)d)+(n-1)b^(-d), d=r(b-a), was independently rederived.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Coronel--Huancas (2014) states Conjecture 3.3 for all n, x_i in (0,1], and r in [0,e]. Matejicka (2016) explicitly reports Conjectures 3.1 and 3.2 invalid but does not state a resolution of 3.3. Searches by the numbered conjecture, exact authors/title, product formulation, and later citation chains through 2026 found no published all-dimensional counterexample family. The 2016 paper's displayed point for a different cyclic inequality also appears on substitution to violate 3.3, so this record does not claim priority for the first isolated counterexample; its originality claim is the exact uniform family for every n>=2 and the complete dimension-wise resolution.

value.summary: The result closes the remaining numbered sequence conjecture from the 2014 paper as a universal statement, and does so uniformly in every nontrivial dimension with one fixed r and two fixed coordinate values. The two-level reduction also exposes a simple mechanism generating open sets of counterexamples.

limitations: The full parameter region of validity and failure is not classified.
The two-level criterion is not a characterization of all counterexamples.
No priority claim is made for the first isolated counterexample because a 2016 published data point for another inequality also appears to violate Conjecture 3.3.
A differently phrased or non-indexed prior all-dimensional family may exist.
Independent audit has not been performed.
